extra.message: The username value from the request body (sqli.get('username') on line 10) is concatenated directly into a SQL query string via an f-string and executed with cur.execute(). There is no parameterization or sanitization, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. username=' OR '1'='1) to bypass authentication and read/modify the USERS table.

User-supplied input (ssti.get('mathexp') on line 9) is concatenated into a Jinja2 template string and then rendered with test.render() on line 12. Because the attacker controls the template source, they can inject template directives such as {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }} leading to arbitrary code execution on the server.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code (Code Injection)

extra.message: The filename from the request body (lfi.get('filename') on line 13) is passed unsanitized to fetchfile(), which calls open(name).read() (line 3) with no path validation. An attacker can supply traversal sequences (e.g. ../../../../etc/passwd) to read arbitrary files on the server filesystem.

The imagelink value from the request body (rfi.get('imagelink') on line 15) is passed unsanitized to fetchimage(), which calls requests.get(url=name) (line 5). An attacker can make the server issue HTTP requests to arbitrary targets, including internal services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/) or localhost admin interfaces, enabling Server-Side Request Forgery.

The username from the request body (xss.get('username') on line 7) is reflected directly into the response message via an f-string with no escaping or sanitization. If a client renders the 'msg' field as HTML, an attacker can inject <script> payloads resulting in reflected Cross-Site Scripting.

The Host request header (headerss['Host'] on line 12) is reflected unsanitized into the response body inside an HTML anchor: <a href='{h}'>. An attacker who controls the Host header can break out of the attribute (e.g. x'><script>alert(1)</script>) to inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript, resulting in reflected Cross-Site Scripting via an HTTP header.

requests.get() is called with verify=False, which disables TLS certificate validation. This makes the outbound request vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks, allowing an attacker to intercept or tamper with the fetched content.

The Flask/Connexion application is started with debug=True bound to host 0.0.0.0. Debug mode enables the Werkzeug interactive debugger, which exposes detailed stack traces (source code disclosure) and, if the debugger PIN is obtained, allows arbitrary remote code execution. This must never be enabled in a network-accessible deployment.

When the SQL query raises an exception, the raw exception message is returned directly to the client in the response (return {"msg": f"{e}"}). Database error messages can reveal internal schema, table, and column names, aiding an attacker in crafting further attacks.

cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through an Error Message

extra.message: The entire set of HTTP request headers is printed to the application log (print(f"headers: {headerss}")). Request headers may contain sensitive data such as Authorization tokens or Cookies, which would then be persisted in logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: User credentials are hardcoded in the database setup script, including a privileged 'admin' account with password 'admin' (line 28) and a 'mike' account with password 'kaines' (line 25). Hardcoded, weak, well-known credentials allow trivial authentication bypass against the login endpoint.
